lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - A Listen and say. Then practise. Audio track 23 and 24

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pron of the food items. Then practise allow students to repeat given words in a structured question and answer.
Look for careful listening, clear pronunciation of food words, and confident repetition of the question and answer.
“I’m at school and I’m so hungry! Look — these are the foods in the cafeteria today. Mmm… chicken, rice, noodles… everything looks delicious! Let’s listen and say the words together.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - B. Ask and answer Audio track 25

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for accurate use of ‘What does he/she want?” questions and confident sentence answers with consistent reference to the food and boy/girl in the picture.
“I still can’t decide — maybe my friends can help. What does Amy want? What does Nick want? Let’s ask and answer so I can see what everyone else is eating.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - A Look and Circle

details: Look and circle tests students’ understanding and recognition of words.
Look for word recognition skills and neat circling in students’ books.
“I’m trying to choose, but I keep changing my mind. Should I pick something big? Something sweet? Something healthy? Let’s look at the pictures and check the words — maybe that will help me think.”

Heads Up:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - B Look and Write

details: Look and write tests students’ ability to write a word correctly using given letter clues and visuals.
Look for good recognition of visual to written words. Also ability to spell words correctly and neat writing inside the crossword squares.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - Speaking Circle 3 things. Make a group

details: Circle 3 and make a group allows students autonomy to create their food wish list and form a group for speaking task.
Look for ability to decide on 3 food items out of 6 and neat circling, as well as social skills in forming a group with other students.
“Okay, time to choose! Let’s circle the three foods you want most. I’m thinking about size, taste, and what I feel like today… maybe that will help me decide. You choose yours too!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - Choose roles. Act out Restaurant Scene

details: Choose roles and act out creates semi-controlled practice for students in a fun way. They practise speaking and writing depending on their role.
Look for use of ‘What do you want?’ questions and clear sentence answers,
“Oh no — I’m first in line now! I have to choose quickly before everyone is waiting behind me. Tell me: what do you want? Let’s act it out so we can order fast!”

Read, listen and sing provides the opportunity to recognise the target structure and vocabulary in a song as well as practising reading and listening skills.
Look for accurate reading as well as good pronunciation as students follow the lyrics and finally sing the song as a group.
“Mmm! I finally chose — I picked the pizza, and I’m so glad I did. It’s my favourite! Let’s sing our song together to celebrate our delicious choices today.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Sing): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video Song):
